readings_ruling: The crux: the 'false as printed' finding is CORRECT. Déf. 1′ (transcription l.119–145; checked against the scan's page image, journal p. 247 = PDF p. 20) requires « une fonction linéaire z, appelée cote, sur H̊ considéré comme espace affin » and, as condition a, « Sur l'image φ(P), la cote z a pour borne inférieure 0 et est majorée par 1 ». The zero function is a « fonction linéaire » under every reading: affine, or homogeneous linear form as in the examples (« z une forme linéaire »). The constant 0 has infimum 0 on any nonempty φ(P) and is bounded by 1. Condition b holds for (ℝⁿ, H₀, j, 0), which is a pocket in the paper's own sense. Take P = ℝⁿ. Every segment of ℝⁿ for its canonical projective structure is an affine segment, and φ̃ = j on it, so φ̃(M, N) ⊂ H₀. Also z(φ̃(N)) = 0 < 1 and N ∈ ℝⁿ = P. No sentence of Chapter 2 excludes z ≡ 0. Condition a says « borne inférieure », not « non atteinte ». The Théorème of § 3 (l.517–533) says « l'ensemble des points de H̊ où z<1 », which is meaningful for z ≡ 0. Prop. 7 and its proof only need B ∈ P. The strict Benzecri.IsPocheProj (Poches.lean:585–597) is literal on this point. Its SCOPE (l.106–107) already says « Constant cotes are allowed (the paper does not exclude them) ». So the strict Déf. 1′ is NOT broader than the printed Déf. 1′, and its mark (LEDGER row bzdef:c2s1d1prime_poche_projective, strict, yes) is correct for the print. The conclusions are strict « < » on the scan: page images of journal p. 249 (7°: « N∈P et z φ(N) < K z(φ(M)) ») and p. 252 (Prop. 6: « z(φ(B)) < K^p z(φ(A)) »). The same page 249 prints ≦ in 1°, 3°, 4° and 5°, so the < is deliberate. With z ≡ 0 the printed conclusions read 0 < 0, for every segment: in ℝⁿ every segment has l_V = 0, so the degenerate point segment the Lean witness uses is not needed. The paper does, however, TACITLY presuppose a non-constant cote, and the REPORT does not say so (finding 1). The examples and the announcement after them build P from « le demi-espace ouvert z<1 » (l.158, l.165–166, l.174, l.186), which is a half-space only when z is non-constant. The proof of 7° writes 0<z(f) (l.351) and closes the case z(b) ≤ z(a) (l.346–348) with no inequality, which needs z(a) > 0. So the defect sits most plausibly in Déf. 1/1′ (an omitted non-degeneracy), and the REPORT's correction (a) is the reading the text supports. Other readings. « ligne brisée » as p ≥ 1 chained segments, each majorised by k in V, with support their union and with no requirement to stay in E: sound. For Prop. 4 a p = 0 « line » would only make the conclusion easier, and the Lean proves the p ≥ 1 form. For Prop. 6, p = 0 must be excluded (z(φ(A)) < z(φ(A))), as the REPORT notes. « ainsi que L » as L ⊆ P, L the support: the natural reading. « connexe » as IsPreconnected E with M ∈ E: equivalent to connected for nonempty E, a weakening. « K supérieur à 1 » (7°) read 1 < K in SeptiemeProprietePrinted: equivalent to 1 ≤ K for the printed predicate, because K = 1 makes l_V < log 1 = 0 impossible.

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d5_nombre_recouvrement
labels.notes: Correctly UNMARKED, status partial (OQ-45, [NeZero n] disclosed as ⚠ strengthened). Benzecri.nombreRecouvrement n k E (Lignes.lean:157) is sInf {m | ∃ O : Fin m → Set V, IsRecouvrementMajore n k E O}. IsRecouvrementMajore (l.147) is: each O i open and IsMajorePart n k (O i) (strict Déf. 4, Mesure.lean:304, majorised in V), and E ⊆ ⋃ O i. This is « un recouvrement de E, formé de n ouverts majorés par k ». Repetitions and empty members are harmless: deleting duplicates or empties gives a covering of no greater size, so the least m is the same under the « n distinct open sets » reading. Junk value: sInf ∅ = 0 occurs only when no covering exists. In the paper's domain (E compact, k > 0, n ≥ 1) exists_isRecouvrementMajore (Prop. 3 via exists_isOpen_isMajorePart, then elim_nhds_subcover) gives a covering, and nombreRecouvrement_isLeast proves IsLeast, so the value is the paper's « le plus petit entier ». A junk 0 could never make Prop. 4 vacuously true either: p ≤ 0 is impossible for a broken line (IsLigneBrisee.one_le). n(∅, k) = 0 is the paper's value (the empty family covers ∅). Dimension 0: exists_isRecouvrementMajore_dim_zero_iff (a part has a covering iff it is empty) rests on not_isMajorePart_dim_zero, that is on Déf. 1's convention (no measure for coincident points), as in the T-bz-c2-hilbert audit. That is OQ-45, which the REPORT routes correctly. Routing: under OQ-45 (a), mark Benzecri.nombreRecouvrement with nombreRecouvrement_isLeast as its certificate.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p4_ligne_brisee
labels.notes: Correctly UNMARKED, status partial (OQ-45). Benzecri.ligne_brisee (Lignes.lean:476) takes [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] [NeZero n] (disclosed), E compact, IsPreconnected E (⚠ weakened, with M ∈ E equivalent to connected), 0 < k (implicit in the paper through Déf. 5), and M, N ∈ E. It concludes ∃ p L, p ≤ nombreRecouvrement n k E ∧ IsLigneBrisee n k p M N L. IsLigneBrisee (l.166) is inductive: one segment majorised by k in V (IsMajoreSeg, strict Déf. 2), or such a segment followed by a line. isLigneBrisee_iff proves it equivalent to the vertex form: p ≥ 1, X 0 = M, X p = N, Sg i majorised from X i to X (i+1), L = ⋃ Sg i. That is « une ligne brisée formée d'au plus n(E, k) segments majorés par k dans V », with nothing added. Not vacuous: S(n) with E a point or a closed segment satisfies the hypotheses. LigneBriseePrinted (l.487) quantifies over every V : Type with the projective groupoid, T2, ConnectedSpace and SecondCountableTopology, every compact connected E, every k > 0 and every M, N ∈ E. That is the printed statement with the standing reading of « variété ». ligneBriseePrinted_iff : LigneBriseePrinted n ↔ 0 < n. Its n = 0 witness is the open set {x} ⊆ S(0), a one-point space that is T2, connected and second countable, and the failure rests on Déf. 1's convention (OQ-45), as disclosed. Proof findings checked against l.393–409. (i) The induction is on n(E, k), but the hypothesis is applied to O_Q, a connected open set for which Déf. 5 defines nothing: true. ligne_brisee_of_finset runs the induction on the size of a finite covering of a preconnected set, as the proof actually needs. (ii) « un tel ouvert est inclus dans O_Q, ou a avec O_Q une intersection vide » needs each O_i connected. That is true by Déf. 4 (IsMajorePart.isPreconnected) and left implicit. The Lean also makes the separation argument explicit (D and B open and disjoint, M ∈ B, N ∈ D). (iii) k used both as the bound and as an index: notation only (line cited wrongly, finding 3). Routing: under OQ-45 (a), mark Benzecri.ligne_brisee as is.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p6_ligne_brisee_poche
labels.notes: Correctly UNMARKED, status partial. The printed statement is false (see readings_ruling), and the CAMPAIGN findings rule (strongest true statement plus a counterexample) is followed. Printed form: LigneBriseePochePrinted n (Lignes.lean:1036) quantifies over every V : Type (projective groupoid, T2, connected, second countable), every pocket IsPocheProj P l φ z (strict Déf. 1′), every A, B, L, p, K with IsLigneBrisee n (log K) p A B L, A ∈ P and z(φ A) < 1/K^p. It concludes L ⊆ P ∧ ∃ B ∈ P, z(φ B) < K^p z(φ A). That is Prop. 6 word for word (« k = log K », « ainsi que L » read as L ⊆ P). SeptiemeProprietePrinted (l.1026) is 7° word for word: 1 < K, M ∈ P, z(φ M) < 1/K, IsProjSegment Sg M N, pseudoLength n Sg M N < log K ⇒ ∃ N ∈ P, z(φ N) < K z(φ M). Witness: exists_isPocheProj_cote_zero is (isPocheAff_model n).toPocheProj e.symm with z = 0 ∘ e, so ∀ y, z y = 0 holds by rfl. This is the Remarque's image of (ℝⁿ, id, 0) on Fin n → ℝ with projOfAff (T2, connected, second countable). The witness segment is {0}, which isProjSegment_singleton and isMajoreSeg_singleton (n ≥ 1) make a segment majorised by log 2. The paper itself treats (M, M) as a segment (1°: l_V(M, M) = 0), and any non-degenerate segment of ℝⁿ (l_V = 0) refutes the print equally. ↔ n = 0: for n = 0 both predicates are vacuous (not_isLigneBrisee_dim_zero, pseudoLength_eq_top_dim_zero). Corrected forms, both true and both kernel-checked. IsPocheProj.ligne_brisee_poche (l.982) adds no hypothesis and takes any real K. It concludes L ⊆ P, B ∈ P, z(φ B) ≤ K^p z(φ A), and < when z(φ A) > 0, a narrower conclusion that is disclosed as the correction. IsPocheProj.ligne_brisee_poche_of_ne_zero (l.1015) adds ∃ y, z y ≠ 0 and gives the printed conclusion. cote_pos_of_ne_zero is correct: φ(P) is open and z ≥ 0 on it, and an affine function with an interior minimum 0 vanishes identically. The K < 0 cases are sound: for p even log K = log(−K) and K^p = (−K)^p, and for p odd the hypothesis is void. Checklist rows 81 and 83 disclose the narrowed conclusion. Proof of Prop. 6 (l.445–449): the REPORT's remark that 7° (l_V < log K) applies to a segment majorised by log K is correct, since the witnessing measure is < log K and chart-independent. The Lean avoids the point with septieme_majore. Routing: question (a) or (b). The evidence for (a) and its effect on the marked Déf. 1/1′ rows are missing from the REPORT (finding 1).

lemmas_checked.IsPocheProj.septieme_propriete: 7° corrected (unmarked, row T-bz-c2-proprietes / OQ-38). Same hypotheses as printed minus K > 1, which is forced (z ≥ 0 makes K ≤ 0 contradict z(φ M) < 1/K, and 0 < K ≤ 1 makes pseudoLength < log K ≤ 0 impossible). IsProjSegment is implied by pseudoLength < ⊤. Conclusion: Sg ⊆ P, N ∈ P, ≤, and < when z(φ M) > 0. This is a stronger conclusion than the printed one apart from the corrected inequality.
lemmas_checked.IsPocheProj.septieme_propriete_of_ne_zer: 7° with the printed conclusion under ∃ y, z y ≠ 0 (correction (a)).
lemmas_checked.IsPocheProj.septieme_majore: The form Prop. 6 uses: Sg majorised by log K instead of l_V < log K. Same conclusions.
lemmas_checked.IsPocheProj.cote_pos_of_ne_zero: z ≢ 0 ⇒ z > 0 on φ(P). This is correct and is the precise sense in which the failure is « exactly the cote 0 ».
lemmas_checked.septieme_alg, Sphere.exists_linear_cote,: General lemmas, stated correctly. An affine function on H̊ is Λ/l. Along a segment of H̊ the cote lies between its endpoint values. The real inequality behind 7°.

findings.what: The finding that 7° and Prop. 6 are false as printed is correct. But the REPORT does not give the author the textual evidence that the paper tacitly assumes a non-constant cote, nor what correction (a) costs. Evidence: the examples and the announcement after them build P from « le demi-espace ouvert z<1 » (l.158, l.165–166, l.174, l.186), which is a half-space only for z non-constant. The proof of 7° writes 0<z(f) (l.351) and closes the case z(b) ≤ z(a) (l.346–348) with no inequality, which needs z(a) > 0. The defect therefore sits most plausibly in Déf. 1/1′ (an omitted non-degeneracy) rather than in 7° and Prop. 6. Cost: under (a) the change falls on two MARKED strict rows, bzdef:c2s1d1_poche_affine and bzdef:c2s1d1prime_poche_projective. IsPocheAff and IsPocheProj would gain a field. isPocheAff_model and exists_isPocheProj_model (z = 0, today's non-vacuity witnesses, Poches.lean:1297, 1312) would no longer be pockets, and exists_isCoqueStricteAff_demiDroite / exists_isCoqueStricteProj_demiDroite would remain the witnesses. The strict definition is faithful to the print as it stands, so nothing is wrong today. Only the author's choice is under-informed.

Under (a), the marked strict Déf. 1 and Déf. 1′ (IsPocheAff, IsPocheProj) gain the field ∃ y, z y ≠ 0. isPocheAff_model and exists_isPocheProj_model stop being witnesses, and the demi-droite strict shells replace them. Under (b) the strict library is unchanged.'

findings.what: « les quatre points a, b, f, f′ ont une cote z positive » (l.343) is said to 'fail for z ≡ 0'. That holds only if « positive » means > 0. Benzécri writes « strictement positif » when he means > 0 (l.366, l.383, l.470), so the French convention positif = ≥ 0 is available, and under it the sentence is TRUE for z ≡ 0, where all four cotes are 0. Under that reading it is true for every pocket: z ≥ 0 at b, f, f′ follows from condition b on sub-segments, which is the argument the REPORT itself supplies. What is unconditionally true is that the sentence is asserted without argument, and that the case z(b) ≤ z(a) needs z(a) > 0. The sub-claim concerns the proof, not the statement, and the main finding does not depend on it. But as worded it would reach the author as a fact.
findings.fix: Replace 'is asserted without argument and fails for z = 0' with 'is asserted without argument. Read as ≥ 0 it holds for every pocket, by condition b on the sub-segments (M, X). Read as > 0, as 0<z(f) at l.351 suggests, it fails for z ≡ 0.' Make the same change in REPORT labels[2].findings[2].
